raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

With `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec`, KDA allocates its speculative ReplaySSM ring for every Mamba slot, but each verify only writes the running requests' rows, and the same step's commit folds them. On GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 at TP2 with 512 Mamba slots and 64 running requests, the ring takes 12.8 GB per GPU.

## Modifications

- Allocate the KDA spec ring with one row per running request, including on PD decode servers, and charge it to the KV pool as fixed request scratch.
- Index the ring by the verify scratch row that `intermediate_conv_window` uses: `intermediate_state_indices` during verify and `src_indices_raw` at commit (the batch row, or the request row under PP). The unfused kernel takes it as an optional `ring_indices` (note that `ring_indices` defaults to the state slot, so GDN's call doesn't change).
- Require `--speculative-algorithm` with `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec`, since the ring is now sized by `--max-running-requests`, which can't be `None`.
- Describe the ring as per request in the Kimi-K3 cookbook.

## Accuracy Tests

GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 on 2xB200 with a DFlash2 draft, 512 Mamba slots, 64 running requests, and ring length 16:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Spec ring per GPU | 12.8 GB | 1.63 GB |
| KV cache tokens | 647,680 | 1,637,120 |
| GSM8K | 0.930 | 0.930 |
| Accept length | 5.07 | 5.07 |

Both arms allocate the unused `d`/`k` rings that #45509 removes. With both PRs, the ring takes 1.08 GB per GPU.

New pool tests check that the KDA spec ring holds the accounted bytes per running request, on a regular and a PD decode server. The backend verify-commit test now sizes its rings by request. The ring, fold, fused verify, and CuTe DSL tests pass on CPU (39), 1xH200 (78), and 1xB200 (10).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The compute path is unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

 - `S` — KDA state slots per request: `extra_buffer=5`, `extra_buffer_lazy=4`, `no_buffer=3`, disabled radix cache `=1`. `SGLANG_OPT_MAMBA_SKIP_DECODE_LOCK` frees one slot on the extra-buffer strategies; with the overlap scheduler off (or `pp > 1`, which disables it) the track buffer costs one slot instead of two.
-- `D` — verify intermediate states under speculative decoding: `0` when disabled, otherwise DSPARK block size + 1 (`8` at the default 7). ReplaySSM (`--enable-linear-replayssm-spec`) folds them into a per-slot ring, returning `D` to `0`.
+- `D` — verify intermediate states under speculative decoding: `0` when disabled, otherwise DSPARK block size + 1 (`8` at the default 7). ReplaySSM (`--enable-linear-replayssm-spec`) folds them into a per-request ring, returning `D` to `0`.
 - `state_bytes` — one state slot's bytes, from K3's fixed geometry, the attention-TP width, and the SSM dtype.
 - `mla_kv_bytes` — one token's MLA latent KV bytes (KV-dtype dependent); DCP shards it across its ranks. The DSPARK draft model's KV (~1.4 KB per token) is replicated on every rank, so it enters flat — negligible without DCP, the same order as the sharded MLA share under DCP8.
 - `L` — average total request length in tokens: input + output.
